$comment: Azure Static Web Apps config for the preview origin. Deploy ONLY runner.html, the csharp-runner/ folder (with _framework/ from `npm run build:csharp`) and the sql-runner/ folder (worker.js and sql.js, emitted by `npm run build`) here, never the app. The header CSP intersects with the meta CSP inside each page, so it can only tighten it: set img-src to your media CDN. csharp-runner/ gets its own CSP: its Web Worker loads .NET from this origin (connect-src 'self', 'wasm-unsafe-eval'), and the header is the worker's only CSP. sql-runner/ gets the same CSP for the same reason (its worker loads SQLite's .wasm). The .NET and SQLite file names aren't fingerprinted, so they're revalidated (no-cache) rather than cached forever.

headers.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors https://app.codegrove.example
default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; worker-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors https://app.codegrove.example

globalHeaders.Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data: blob: https://media.codegrove.example; font-src data:; media-src data: blob:; connect-src 'none'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors https://app.codegrove.example
